---
title: "Engineering log"
---

Design decisions, refactors, numerical stability issues, data layout and
performance choices. It supplements the git history with the reasoning.
Entries are dated H2 sections; existing entries are never edited.

## 2026-11-05: Step 0, project scaffolding

**Double precision.** `jax_enable_x64` is set in `jaxdft/_config.py`, the
first import in `jaxdft/__init__.py`. Any entry point that imports anything
from the package therefore enables x64 before any array exists. The test suite
checks this in a fresh subprocess as well as in-process, because
`tests/conftest.py` imports `jaxdft` for every test and would otherwise hide a
broken import order.

`jaxdft.precision.assert_double_precision` walks a pytree and rejects any
inexact leaf that is not float64 or complex128. Integer and boolean leaves
(Miller indices, masks) are ignored. Physics tests should call it on their
outputs. This is how "a test must fail if any physical array is float32" is
enforced in practice.

**Test configuration.**

- `--import-mode=importlib`, so the three test directories can contain
  files with the same name without `__init__.py` packages.
- `filterwarnings = error`: a warning from JAX (e.g. an implicit dtype
  truncation) fails the test rather than scrolling past.
- `--strict-markers`, with one marker, `slow`, defined up front.
- Hypothesis runs with `deadline=None`, because the first call of a jitted
  function includes tracing and compilation, so per-example timing is
  meaningless. Two profiles: `default` (50 examples, for laptops) and `ci`
  (200), selected with `HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE`.

**Dependencies.** `pytest` and `hypothesis` are in the `dev` group, `altair`
and `jupyter` in `docs`. Both are uv default groups, since the definition of
done needs both, so a plain `uv sync` installs everything.

**Docs execution.** `execute.freeze` is explicitly `false`. Documents compute
their numbers from `jaxdft` at render time, and freezing would let a document
go stale against the code without failing.

Quarto must find the project's virtual environment. It does when the venv is
active (it then picks `.venv/bin/python3` from `PATH`). From a plain shell it
falls back to the system Python and fails. I tried a `docs/_environment` file
setting `QUARTO_PYTHON`. Quarto resolves that relative path against the
directory it is invoked from, not the project, so it broke depending on where
the command was run, and I removed it. `uv run quarto render docs/` works from
any shell and is the robust form of the definition-of-done command.

**Removed.** The `jaxdft` console-script entry point and its `main()`
placeholder from the `uv init` template. A command-line interface will be
added when there is something to run.

**Deferred.**

- The shared plot-style module arrives with the first plot (Milestone 1a
  validation). It will live outside the physics so that `altair` stays a docs
  dependency.
- A `units` module with tested conversions arrives with the first
  boundary conversion. Milestone 1a works entirely in atomic units and in
  units of $\tfrac12(2\pi/a)^2$.

## 2026-11-05: Milestone 1a design decisions from theory review

The [theory post](../theory/01a_empty_lattice.qmd) was reviewed before any
implementation. Every quantitative claim was re-derived independently, and no
physics errors were found. The review changed four engineering decisions.
I reproduced its measurements with a throwaway NumPy enumeration before
accepting them.

**Per-k padded Miller-index lists, not a shared candidate set.** `vmap` needs
a common shape, not a common set of G vectors. The first draft proposed one
set containing every $\mathcal{B}_\mathbf{k}$ (radius $G_\text{max} + |\mathrm{W}|$)
plus a per-k mask. For fcc with $a = 10.26$ Bohr over the six high-symmetry
points, that set was 1.73× the largest per-k basis at 5 Ha and 1.17× at 80 Ha.
Dense `eigh` costs the cube of that: 5.1× and 1.6×. The per-k sizes
themselves differ by about 2%. The batch layout is therefore
`(n_k, N_pad, 3)` integer Miller indices plus an `(n_k, N_pad)` boolean mask.
`N_pad` is a Python int fixed on the host before tracing. These numbers are a
one-off snapshot for the decision record; the validation document computes
them from the library.

**Padding is exactly decoupled, and the sentinel is modest.** Padded components
must have zero rows and columns, not just a large diagonal. Otherwise
$\tilde V(\mathbf{G}-\mathbf{G}')$ in 1b, evaluated at a padding entry's
arbitrary Miller index, would leak into the physical block. The sentinel
diagonal is a small multiple of $E_\text{cut}$. The reviewer measured that LAPACK's
physical eigenvalues are insensitive to the sentinel (1.9e-13 Ha for sentinels
from 4e1 to 1e12). A huge sentinel would still spread the spectrum over many
orders of magnitude, which slows down the iterative solvers planned later.
The test is solver-independent: the same k-point with two values of `N_pad`
must give the same bands.

**Provable enumeration bound.** The integer search box is
$|m_i| \le \lceil (G_\text{max}+|\mathbf{k}|)|\mathbf{a}_i|/2\pi \rceil$, from
$\mathbf{G}\cdot\mathbf{a}_i = 2\pi m_i$ and Cauchy–Schwarz. A guessed cube is
unsafe in skewed cells.

**Cutoff ties.** Test cutoffs are placed strictly between shells, with a
relative margin of at least 1e-8. The reviewer suggested instead making the
reference enumeration use the code's own arithmetic, so ties round the same
way. I did not adopt that, because it makes the reference less independent of
the code it checks.

**Basis-size bound.** The reviewer flagged that a test asserting monotone
convergence of $N_\text{PW}$ to its asymptote would be flaky, and proposed a
bound $C\,E_\text{cut}^{-1/2}$ with $C$ measured once. I used a rigorous bound
instead, from tiling with Brillouin zones of circumradius $r_\text{BZ}$, which
needs no fitted constant. A first version used the reciprocal parallelepiped's
diameter (2.03 Bohr⁻¹ at $a = 10.26$). It held, but was nearly vacuous: the
upper bound was 4.4 at 5 Ha. The Wigner–Seitz circumradius $|\mathrm{W}|$
(0.68 Bohr⁻¹) is three times tighter. It is still loose and catches only
gross errors; the exact count is tested by enumeration.

**References.** Cutoff conventions as documented for DFTK (`Ecut`), ABINIT
(`ecut`) and Quantum ESPRESSO (`ecutwfc`, `ecutrho`). No source code was
consulted.
